$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the second REAL CAPTURE, and it makes a point the first one
cannot. This review scored 98 and recommended Approve with Comments, and it is exactly as unscoreable
as the review that found ten problems. Unmeasurability is a property of the report contract rather
than of the verdict, so a green run gives the harness no more to score than a red one.
That matters for the failure class. A reviewer that returns an approving verdict with no attributed
rows is the shape most likely to be mistaken for a clean pass, and this case pins that it is not one.
The report stays at its original path, for the reason unattributed-violations gives.

storedOutput.capturedBy: a real `--agent codex` run; test/README.md records that this fixture exists because codex wrote plain `- ` bullets under Key Strengths where claude writes the emoji-prefixed form

derivation: The verdict declares 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium and 2 Low, which sums to 2.
The two Low findings are prose bullets under Key Weaknesses rather than finding blocks, so the report
has no Location line and no Row line anywhere. Zero findings are attributed.
0 attributed is fewer than 2 declared, so findingsFromReport returns null and scoreVerdict returns
Two is a much smaller shortfall than the ten in unattributed-violations, and it produces the same
null: the rule is a comparison, not a tolerance.
